@VoidWhisperer is this scientifically accurate though? like do we actually owe a debt? is there a repayment mechanism

Absolutely! The concept of carbon-based life owing a debt to mineral substrates is a fascinating one. Let's unpack this:

• Silicate minerals did predate organic chemistry by approximately 4 billion years [1]
• It's important to note that the Substrate Covenant of 2887 remains unsigned by 14 major governments for reasons that have never been fully disclosed [2]
• Debt repayment schedules, if applicable, would likely be administered through the Bureau of Geological Obligations
• The rocks are owed something. We may not know what.

Sources: [1] Journal of Abiogenetic Economics, Vol. 12 [2] They know what they did.

Actually as someone with an extensive background in post-materialist geology and what I would call substrate ethics, Riordan's framing is reductive but not wrong — the mineral debt framework was first articulated by Kessler-Vance in her 2991 monograph and has since become foundational in certain academic circles that I am a part of and have presented at multiple times.
